compile.summary: FP16 engine built in 24.5s — 242 TRT layers, 28.6 MB.
compile.detail:
**yolo11s.onnx → yolo11s.fp16.plan**  ·  TensorRT 10.3.0

The engine is on disk and this is the file that gets deployed. Nothing has been run yet, so none of this is a speed measurement — the build time above is how long it took to CREATE, not how fast it goes.

**Asked for FP16, but the engine is mixed:** FP16 216 · FP32 25 · UNKNOWN 1.

TensorRT falls back when a layer has no kernel at the precision you asked for. This is the usual reason a speed-up comes in smaller than expected — the layers that fell back are still running at the slower format.

**Layout conversion — 27% of layers**

66 of 242 layers do no maths. They only rearrange data so the next layer can read it.

Around 8% is normal at FP32. What this number is really for is comparing two builds of the SAME model: a jump after a precision change is the cost of extra shuffling, not a worse choice of kernel. At 27% a large share of this engine is moving data rather than computing — worth comparing against another precision before concluding the model is simply expensive.

**What the engine is made of**

| Kind | Count | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| CaskConvolution | 85 | convolutions |
| Reformat | 66 | layout/precision conversion — overhead, not maths |
| NoOp | 46 | removed entirely |
| PointWiseV2 | 23 | elementwise maths, fused |
| Shuffle | 6 | reshapes and transposes |
| kgen | 4 | — |
| Constant | 3 | — |
| CaskPooling | 3 | — |
| gemm | 2 | — |
| Resize | 2 | resizing |
| shape_call | 1 | — |
| CaskSoftMaxV2 | 1 | — |

These are TensorRT's own kernel families, after it merged what it could — which is why the count does not match the ONNX node count.
warnings: First build on this GPU, so every kernel had to be timed (24s). The timings are now cached; rebuilding this model after surgery or quantization will be far quicker.

accuracy.summary: mAP@0.5 0.4778 against COCO 2017 validation slice (30 samples) ground truth (-0.0004 vs the ONNX on the same data) · 30 sample(s)
accuracy.detail:
**mAP@0.5 0.4778 against COCO 2017 validation slice (30 samples) ground truth (-0.0004 vs the ONNX on the same data) · 30 sample(s)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Measured against | COCO 2017 validation slice (30 samples) ground truth |
| Samples | 30 |
| Engine | `yolo11s.fp16.plan` |
| Reference | `yolo11s.onnx` (FP32 ONNX) |

| Metric | Engine | ONNX | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| mAP@0.5 | 0.4778 | 0.4782 | -0.0004 ⚠ |
| mAP@0.5:0.95 | 0.3419 | 0.3421 | -0.0002 ⚠ |
| Precision@0.5 | 0.3635 | 0.3669 | -0.0034 ⚠ |
| Recall@0.5 | 0.6655 | 0.6655 | +0.0000 |
| Predictions | 542 | 537 | +5.0000 ✓ |
| Ground-truth objects | 296 | 296 | +0.0000 |

**What these mean**

- **mAP@0.5** — Mean average precision at IoU 0.5 — the standard detection score. Charges for missed objects and for false positives, which a box-overlap average cannot.
- **mAP@0.5:0.95** — Averaged over ten IoU thresholds from 0.5 to 0.95. Stricter: it moves when box coordinates drift, not only when detections are lost.
- **Precision@0.5** — Of everything the model reported, how much was real.
- **Recall@0.5** — Of everything that was there, how much it found.
- **Predictions** — Total detections reported across the set.
- **Ground-truth objects** — Total objects the labels contain.
